title: How do we zoom in to find four point one eight five?
description: A number line is zoomed again and again, one digit at a time, to locate 4.185 and to read the decimal marked with a question mark. Keeko doubts the place of 4.185 and thinks it is near 4.15.
teaching_notes: One idea: each digit after the point gives the next zoom, and each zoom cuts a gap into ten equal parts. Watch for students who round the number in their head instead of following the digits.

source: Locate 4.185 by zooming. Then read the decimal marked '?' in
video_script.why: The child can place tenths and hundredths on a line and now zooms again for thousandths.
video_script.substitution: Follow the digits one by one, and each digit gives the gap to zoom into next.
video_script.anchor: the zoomed number lines of the book, magnified at each level to locate 4.185
video_script.wrong_move: Thinks 4.185 is near 4.15 and so looks in the wrong gap.
video_script.payoff_line: Each digit gives the next zoom

final_answer.value: 4.185 is the middle mark of 4.18 to 4.19; '?' is 3.059
final_answer.spoken: four point one eight five is the middle mark of four point one eight to four point one nine; the question mark is three point zero five nine

hold_back: 4.185 is the middle mark of 4.18 to 4.19; '?' is 3.059
maths_rules: 4.185: units digit 4 gives the gap 4 to 5
thousandths digit 5 gives the 5th of 10 parts, the middle mark 4.185
video_script.design: The book's zoom lines stay on screen and grow one level at a time. One colour marks the chosen gap, another marks the final mark.
open_questions: The worklist gives the zoom path for the question mark as 3 to 4, 3.0 to 3.1, 3.05 to 3.06 and the 9th mark; the book's own figure labels are not readable in the text.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Where does four point one eight five sit?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the end of the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: zoom = cut one gap into 10 equal parts and look at one part; each digit gives the next zoom

marks.zoom: one gap is cut into ten equal parts

narration: <bookmark mark='zoom'/>To zoom is to cut one gap into ten equal parts, and look at one part.
<bookmark mark='dig'/>Each digit after the point tells us which part to look at next.
<bookmark mark='nest'/>A new digit gives a new zoom, and each zoom is ten times smaller.

beats.on_screen: Given: the decimal 4.185; a zoom 3 to 4, then 3.0 to 3.1, then 3.05 to 3.06, ending at the 9th of 10 parts

marks.zoomq: the three gaps of the second zoom are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the decimal four point one eight five.
<bookmark mark='zoomq'/>Also a zoom from three to four, then three to three point one.
The last zoom runs from three point zero five to three point zero six.
<bookmark mark='ninth'/>The question mark is the ninth of ten parts in the last gap.

beats.on_screen: To find: the place of 4.185; the decimal at '?'
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to place four point one eight five by zooming.
<bookmark mark='find2'/>We also read the decimal at the question mark.

beats.on_screen: 4.185: units digit 4, gap 4 to 5; tenths digit 1, gap 4.1 to 4.2

marks.u: the units digit lights up and the gap four to five is chosen
marks.t: the tenths digit lights up and the next zoom opens

narration: <bookmark mark='u'/>Step one, the units digit is four. The gap is from four to five.
<bookmark mark='t'/>The tenths digit is one, so zoom into four point one to four point two.

beats.on_screen: hundredths digit 8, gap 4.18 to 4.19; thousandths digit 5, the 5th of 10 parts

marks.h: the hundredths digit lights up and the gap opens

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step two, the hundredths digit is eight. Zoom into four point one eight to four point one nine.
<bookmark mark='th'/>The thousandths digit is five, so take the fifth of the ten parts.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>That mark is four point one eight five, right in the middle.

beats.on_screen: '?': zoom 3 to 4, units 3; zoom 3.0 to 3.1, tenths 0; zoom 3.05 to 3.06, hundredths 5
narration: <bookmark mark='q1'/>Step three, read the question mark. The first zoom runs from three to four.
The units digit is three.
<bookmark mark='q2'/>The second zoom runs from three to three point one. The tenths digit is zero.
<bookmark mark='q3'/>The third zoom runs from three point zero five to three point zero six.
The hundredths digit is five.

marks.add: nine thousandths are added to three point zero five

narration: <bookmark mark='n'/>Step four, the mark is the ninth part in a gap of ten parts. Each part is one thousandth.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Three point zero five plus zero point zero zero nine gives three point zero five nine.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4.185 is the middle mark of 4.18 to 4.19; '?' is 3.059

marks.q: the question mark turns into its decimal

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each digit gives the next zoom.
<bookmark mark='place'/>Four point one eight five is the middle mark. The gap is four point one eight to four point one nine.
<bookmark mark='q'/>The question mark is three point zero five nine.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the zoom lines
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.fix: the gap from 4.1 to 4.2 is outlined
marks.dig: the digit 8 sends the zoom to 4.18 to 4.19

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four point one eight five is near four point one five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four point one five lies in the gap from four point one to four point two.
<bookmark mark='dig'/>The digit eight sends us to the gap from four point one eight to four point one nine.
